request: The CRM should alert us when our relationship with a country goes cold.
gaps: Who exactly can configure the user-defined settings for the cold relationship duration?
What happens when a user leaves the organization or changes roles regarding alert access?
How will the engagement history data be validated for accuracy and completeness?
What types of engagements are included in the logging system?
Which specific users or roles will have access to view the cold relationship dashboard widget?

proposals.summary: This release will implement an alerting feature within the Government CRM that notifies users when there has been no engagement with a specific country contact for a defined period. The feature will primarily serve regional coordinators and project managers who are responsible for maintaining these relationships.

core_commitments.text: Users will receive automatic alerts when there is no engagement with a country contact for more than 3 months.

in_scope.text: Implement a notification system that triggers an alert when the last engagement date with a country is older than 90 days.
Provide a dashboard widget displaying a list of countries with 'cold' relationships, defined as no engagements in the past 90 days.
Include user-defined settings to customize the duration (threshold) for what is considered a 'cold' relationship up to 180 days.
Allow notifications to be sent via email and in-app messages.
Ensure that only users with appropriate access to country contact data can receive these alerts.
Implement a logging system that records when alerts are triggered, including time and user details.

out_of_scope.text: This release will not include the ability to automate follow-up actions based on alerts.
This release will not alter existing user permissions related to contact data access.
This release will not provide insights or analytics on the nature of engagements.

assumptions.text: Users will have consistent engagement logs for country contacts that can be analyzed for the last engagement date.
assumptions.why_implicit: The feature relies on the availability of accurate and timely logs of engagements.

assumptions.text: Users have a clear understanding of what constitutes an engagement event.
assumptions.why_implicit: Alerts are triggered based on specific engagement criteria that must be defined and understood by users.

assumptions.text: There is an existing method in the CRM for tracking the engagement history of country contacts.
assumptions.why_implicit: The alerting functionality must be based on historical data that is already collected.

assumptions.text: Users are willing to configure their settings regarding what duration they consider 'cold' for relationships.
assumptions.why_implicit: The feature includes user-defined thresholds which rely on user willingness to interact with settings.

definitions.definition: A relationship is defined as 'cold' if there have been no engagements logged with a specific country contact in the past 90 days.
An engagement event refers to any recorded interaction with a country contact, including meetings, emails, or calls.
An alert notification is an automated message sent to users indicating that a specified action needs attention, in this case, a cold relationship alert.

success_criteria.metric: Percentage of cold relationship alerts that are acknowledged by users within 48 hours of being sent.
success_criteria.measurement: This will be tracked through CRM notification response metrics.

C1.challenge: S1 states that users will receive alerts when there has been no engagement for more than 3 months, but it does not specify who can see these alerts, potentially exposing sensitive diplomatic relationships to unauthorized users.
C1.failure_scenario: A project manager receives alerts about cold contacts for a country that they are not authorized to engage with, leading to potential diplomatic missteps and breaches of confidentiality.
C1.resolution_test: Which specific roles can receive alerts for cold relationships?

C2.resolution_test: What specific criteria must engagements meet to be considered valid for the purposes of determining a cold relationship?
